title: Expected AI Path pattern (Story 51.3 AC6)
description: The grammar of an expected AI Path, versioned in the repository rather than inferred from an example. It encodes the six constructs of docs/product-architecture/analyze-and-test.md:271-280, and nothing else: this schema has no field for model reasoning, and migration 150_ai_path_observed_evidence.sql has no column to store it. A pattern is a PATTERN -- it is compared against the immutable observed path, never against a second prose trace.

grammar_version.description: Pins the grammar a stored pattern was written against, so a later widening of this schema cannot silently re-interpret an old Golden Question version.

required_nodes.description: Construct 1. Governed objects that MUST appear in the observed path. A node is identified by owner_workspace + owner_object_type + owner_object_id, the same triple app.ai_path_steps records.

forbidden_nodes.description: Construct 2. Tools, scope changes and shortcuts that FAIL the case when observed. A forbidden node needs no owner_object_id: forbidding a whole object type is legitimate.

order_constraints.description: Construct 4. Declared prerequisites -- 'context inspection before a query', 'DQ inspection before a query'. `before` and `after` are node keys declared in required_nodes; a constraint naming an undeclared key is refused at write time, because a constraint over a node nobody requires can never be violated and would read as satisfied.

alternatives.description: Construct 5. Named alternative branches, ANY ONE of which passes. `analyze-and-test.md:277-278`: a different but allowed call sequence is not penalized. An empty branch list is refused -- 'there are alternatives, and there are none' is not a statement.

extra_step_rules.description: Construct 6. `analyze-and-test.md:279-280`: extra steps matter ONLY when they violate an explicit cost, retry, safety or capability rule declared HERE. With no rule declared, an unexpected step is not a defect and must not be reported as one -- which is why there is no `strict` or `exact_sequence` flag anywhere in this grammar.

exactVersionPin.description: An exact stored version identity. `latest`, `current` and `head` are refused in every letter case, and so is a blank: half a pin pins nothing, and a pattern that followed `latest` would silently change what it asserts.

nodeKey.description: workspace/object_type/object_id -- the stable address of a governed object, matching the triple on app.ai_path_steps.

step_kind.description: Optional narrowing. Absent means any step kind satisfies the node.

owner_version_id.description: Construct 3, governed-object half. Present means the node must appear AT THIS VERSION; a node present at another version is a version mismatch and fails, it is not a missing node.

skill_pin.description: Construct 3, Skill half. Both fields or neither -- the same rule app.ai_path_steps enforces in ck_ai_path_steps_skill_pin. A Skill version without the step it ran is not a pin, it is a hope.

tool.description: Construct 3, tool half. `tool_catalog_version` is compared against the version pinned on the observed path HEADER, which is the catalog that was actually available during the execution.
